questions.stem: What behaviour do Data Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing all refer to?
options: Data analysis performed only on structured tables
Data analysis without a proper hypothesis and relationship among datasets
Data analysis approved by a governance committee
Data analysis that only counts rows
Data analysis restricted to known facts
questions.explanation: Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing all describe analysing data without a proper hypothesis and without an established relationship among the datasets.

questions.stem: How do the findings of Data Mining differ from those of Data Dredging?
options: Data Mining is done by machines; Dredging by humans
Data Mining uses spreadsheets; Dredging uses databases
Data Mining only works on small datasets; Dredging on large ones
Data Mining finds results based on correlation in large datasets; Dredging finds results based on a chance methodology
There is no difference in how they find results
questions.explanation: Data mining finds results based on the correlation of data in large datasets, whereas Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing find results based on chance methodology.

questions.stem: What are the two types of fact findings in any analysis that assists a decision support system?
options: Known facts and unknown facts
Internal facts and external facts
Numeric facts and textual facts
Historical facts and future facts
Approved facts and rejected facts
questions.explanation: There are two types of fact findings: known facts and unknown facts.

questions.stem: Which technique is described as extracting Known Facts because it is done only on structured datasets?
options: Data Fishing
p-hacking
Data Mining
Data Snooping
Data Dredging
questions.explanation: Data mining techniques extract known facts, since they are done on structured datasets where the relationships between and within tables are mostly already known.

questions.stem: In the date-of-birth example, the business rule loads Age only for Male or Female customers aged 1 to 99. What might Data Dredging techniques surface when asked for abnormal age behaviour?
options: Only customers aged exactly 99
Only customers whose gender is Female
Customers born after the current date
Customers with duplicate names
People with no gender defined and an age of more than 500 years
questions.explanation: Dredging searches the age KPI everywhere and may end up showing people who have no gender defined in the system and are aged more than 500 years.

questions.stem: Why is finding customers with abnormal ages described as very critical information?
options: Because it affects the marketing budget
Because it matters for Customer KYC (Know Your Customer)
Because it changes the database schema
Because it invalidates the data warehouse
Because it proves the model has become AI
questions.explanation: The abnormal age finding is described as very critical information for Customer KYC, Know Your Customer.

questions.stem: How are Data Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing generally characterised?
options: As the gold standard of analytics
As a replacement for Business Intelligence
As a form of data backup
As the Dark Side of Data Mining
As a method of data encryption
questions.explanation: The general concept is that these techniques are the Dark Side of Data Mining, although the author treats them as techniques for finding the known and the unknown.

questions.stem: What is the author's own view of Data Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing in I Am Datapedia!?
options: They are techniques for Known and Unknown, and the author is more interested in knowing the Unknown
They should be banned in every organisation
They are identical to Data Mining
They only work on paper records
They are useful only for marketing campaigns
questions.explanation: The author sees them as techniques for Known and Unknown, asks whether knowing the Unknown is bad, and says he is more interested in the Unknown than the Known.

questions.stem: Why have Data Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing become more famous in the Big Data era?
options: Because regulators now require them
Because structured data has disappeared
Because of the new, huge size of semi-structured and unstructured datasets
Because they are built into every database
Because Data Mining is no longer used
questions.explanation: These techniques have become more famous in the Big Data era due to the new, huge size of semi-structured and unstructured datasets.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results of Data Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing is NOT correct?
options: They require more investigation
They sometimes bypass Data Mining techniques
They can come up with immature conclusions
They may show more detail about something than it contains
They never require further investigation
questions.explanation: The results shared by these techniques require more investigation; they sometimes bypass Data Mining techniques, reach immature conclusions and show more than the data contains.
